CITY OF SOUTH GATE
  REGULAR CITY COUNCIL MEETING
  MINUTES
  TUESDAY, AUGUST 22, 2023

CALL TO ORDER  Maria del Pilar Avalos, Mayor called a Regular City Council Meeting to
  order to 6:55 p.m.

INVOCATION  Ernesto Trejo, South Gate Church of Christ
PLEDGE OF
ALLEGIANCE  Yodit Glaze, City Clerk

ROLL CALL  Yodit Glaze, City Clerk

PRESENT  Mayor Maria del Pilar Avalos, Vice Mayor Gil Hurtado, Council Member
  Maria Davila, and Council Member Al Rios; City Treasurer Jose De La
  Paz, City Manager Chris Jeffers, City Attorney Raul F. Salinas

ABSENT/EXCUSED  Council Member Joshua Barron

1
COMMUNITY DEV/
HOUSING  Following the conclusion of the Public Hearing, the City Council
  approved items A, B, C and D by motion of Council Member Davila and
  seconded by Council Member Rios.

  ROLL CALL: Council Member Davila, yes; Council Member Rios, yes;
  Mayor Avalos, yes; Vice Mayor Hurtado, recused; Council Member
  Barron, absent.

  a.  Resolution No. 2023-53-CC entitled Resolution of the City
  Council of the City of South Gate, California, approving
  Substantial Amendment No. 6 to the Fiscal Year 2019-2020
  Annual Action Plan allocating Community Development Block
  Grant Coronavirus ("CDBG-CV3") funds to provide additional
  COVID-19 related programs and services in accordance with the
  U.S. Department of Housing and Urban Development regulations
  (Exhibit A);

  b.  Resolution No. 2023-54-CC entitled Resolution of the City
  Council of the City of South Gate, California, approving
  Substantial Amendment No. 2 to the Fiscal Year 2022-2023
  Annual Action Plan allocating Community Development Block
  Grant ("CDBG") funds to the South Gate Park Fence Project
  (Exhibit B);

  c.  Authorized the City Manager or the Community Development
  Director to enter into agreements with eligible subrecipients and
   REGULAR CITY COUNCIL MEETING MINUTES OF AUGUST 22, 2023

1
COMMUNITY DEV/
HOUSING CONT'D  purchase supplies, programs, and equipment as noted in the FY
  2019-2020 Annual Action Plan; and

  d.  Authorized the City Manager or the Community Development
  Director to enter into agreements with eligible subrecipients and
  purchase supplies, programs, and equipment as noted in the FY
  2022-2023 Annual Action Plan.

  Carol Averall, Housing Manager, went into detail about the CDBF-CV
  changes and the total funds to be re-programmed.

  Ana Ramirez, Southern California Rehabilitation Services, extended
  gratitude for the city council's continue support.

  Resident Mario Dominguez expressed frustration on the sound issues. He
  also requested that funds for homeless people should be increased to
  provide shelter.

  Resident Thomas Buckley addressed concerns of traffic lights being held
  by buckets and how funds should be used to repair roads and lights.

  Cyndi Esquivel asked if there could be roof repair and use of some
  allocated funds for other repairs as well.

  Ms. Averall provided more information on the Home Modification
  program.

  Meredith Elguira, Director of Community Development, provided details
  on the process of fund allocation and what happens if those funds are not
  used.

COMMENTS FROM THE
AUDIENCE (NON-AGENDA
ITEMS)  Daughter of Sandra Beltran, Resident at 3062 Ardmore Ave, voiced issues
  happening in their property of apartment buildings and asked for an
  extension in paying a utility bill as the balance is very high.

  A Vietnam Veteran presented a purple heart frame and asked if it could be
  presented in the city. He also spoke about an issue that happened at
  Hollydale Park where children were exercising their first amendment
  freedom of playing and South Gate PD escorted them out of the park.

  Bill Wallace, 8823 Beaudine Ave, spoke about a petition on a death tax.

  Elaine Julian, resident at Thunderbird Villa, voiced concerns about
  inflation and the rising costs of food in supermarkets.

  Page 2 of 9
   REGULAR CITY COUNCIL MEETING MINUTES OF AUGUST 22, 2023

  COMMENTS FROM THE
  AUDIENCE (NON-AGENDA
  ITEMS) CONT'D  Benito De Los Santos, 2548 Southern Ave, expressed concerns over
  security and safety. He also voiced how the streets need major repairs.

  A resident spoke about an incident where he was playing soccer among
  children and adults. He was told they needed a permit in order to play.

  Resident Bernie Pineda voiced concerns about the Garfield beautification
  project and not being able to make a left turn out of his street. He also
  spoke about the lack of South Gate PD near Los Padrinos Juvenile Center
  and his concerns for safety.

  Resident Mario Dominguez spoke about the minutes and the record. He
  requested that the minutes be taken out of the agenda.

  Resident Thomas Buckley, spoke on behalf of a resident asking what the
  sequence of tree trimming is. He also spoke about the decrease of Senior
  help provided and the need for city council minutes.

  Resident Cyndi Esquivel asked about when the repairs for streets on
  Tweedy would start. She also had questions about funds needed for Boy
  Scouts Huts.

  Resident Andrea Paulino, Hollydale, spoke about credible sources where
  residents can go debunk certain accusations and or facts about the city
  posted on social media.

  Mayor Avalos recognized the purple heart frame and the petition for the
  death tax. She also addressed the help that can be provided for the high
  utility bill for a resident.

  Steve Costley, Interim Director of Parks & Recreation, described the
  permits needed for Hollydale Park and the games taking place. He also
  addressed that some parts of Hollydale are "no ball" play.

  Vice Mayor Hurtado added that it is also a matter of safety for the children
  practicing during those set times.

  Vice Mayor Avalos addressed the help for Seniors being needed and
  wanted to reach out to give the application for the Food Insecurity
  program.

  Arturo Cervantes, Director of Public Works, spoke on the Garfield
  beautification project and announced the date for the discussion of that

I  meeting.

  Page 3 of 9
   REGULAR CITY COUNCIL MEETING MINUTES OF AUGUST 22, 2023
COMMENTS FROM THE
AUDIENCE (NON-AGENDA
ITEMS) CONT'D  Darren Arakawa, Chief of Police, spoke on the safety precautions in
  neighborhoods and the Los Padrinos incident.

  Raul F. Salinas, City Attorney, explained the role of the minutes and why
  it is a crucial record.

  Chris Jeffers, City Manager, was not able to provide a specific date for
  when the Tweedy Mile repairs would take place.

  Mr. Cervantes explained the outreach that would have to take place to
  begin construction. There is no set date, but it is projected to begin 2024.

  Ms. Elguira explained that maintenance is not covered for the CDBG
  funding for roofing of the Boy Scouts.

  Mr. Cervantes explained that there has been funding approved for the Boy
  Scouts Huts through Design.

  Mr. Cervantes addressed the actions of Public Works in aiding to repair
  parts of the city streets.

  Yodit Glaze, City Clerk, recognized the work of the City Clerk's team and
  how there have been no changes in the process of producing the minutes.

  Jose De La Paz, City Treasurer, explained his conversation with Mr.
  Dominguez and future ways that city council meetings can be transcribed
  and recorded.

REPORTS AND COMMENTS
FROM CITY OFFICIALS  Steve Costley, Interim Director of Parks & Recreation announced the
  drive-thru food distribution at South Gate Park.

  Meredith Elguira, Director of Community Development reminded all
  about the food insecurity program and the home renovation program.

  Yodit Glaze, City Clerk described her experience at the City Clerk's
  Summit she attended.

  Wendy O' Kelly, Deputy Director of Finance, expressed gratitude for the
  Department of Finance being awarded the Certificate of Achievement for
  Excellence in Financial Recording.

  Jon Hamilton, Director of Human Resources, went over open positions
  available to apply.

  Page 4 of 9
   REGULAR CITY COUNCIL MEETING MINUTES OF AUGUST 22, 2023

REPORTS AND COMMENTS
FROM CITY OFFICIALS
CONT'D  Darren Arakawa, Chief of Police, recognized Sergeant Carlos Corella for
  graduating from supervisory leadership institute. He also invited everyone
  to attend the Ceremony to recognize recently promoted individuals of the
  Police Department. He also commented on the Pink Patch Dodger game
  and proposed to do a proclamation for the childhood cancer awareness
  month in September in honor of Lily Rose.

  Mayor Avalos supported the proclamation and said it would be an honor
  to give Lily that recognition for her fight against cancer.

  Chris Jeffers, City Manager recognized that tonight was Chief Arakawa's
  Birthday. He also wanted to commend all departments who had a role in
  making sure the city was prepared for the tropical storm.

  Raul F. Salinas, City Attorney, had nothing to report.

  Jose De La Paz, City Treasurer, also echoed Mr. Jeffers' comments on the
  efforts of the departments during the tropical storm. He stated residents
  have reached out over concerns of healthy trees being removed from their
  properties and wanted to ask if there could be a second opinion on cutting
  down certain trees.

  Council Member Davila shared that Metro is asking for ideas in naming
  the West Santa Ana Branch and also her experience at the Northgate
  backpack giveaway. She also extended gratitude for the support and love
  she received when her mother passed last month.

  Council Member Rios acknowledged the Finance Department in their
  award and congratulated them. He also commended the city for their
  efforts in the tropical storm and the Police Department in not using lethal
  force in an incident that happened. He also voiced that tree cutting seems a
  bit aggressive and supports getting a second opinion.

  Vice Mayor Hurtado expressed words of kindness to Council Member
  Davila. He also voiced concerns about tree trimming not being done
  properly and can damage the health of the tree. He followed with the
  impact of streetlights going down resulting in an increase in accidents. He
  is requesting for an increase of patrolling and issuing citations for the
  safety of others. He also commended departments for the tropical storm
  and requested an explanation as to why there was so much flooding in
  front of South Gate High School.

  Mr. Jeffers explained that this was phase 2 of the Firestone improvement
  project and there was no way they could have predicted there would be a
  storm during this time so that resulted in unexpected flooding.

  Page 5 of 9
   REGULAR CITY COUNCIL MEETING MINUTES OF AUGUST 22, 2023

REPORTS AND COMMENTS
FROM CITY OFFICIALS
CONT'D  Vice Mayor Hurtado responded with how people tend to spread
  misinformation and brought up an idea of exploring resources to help
  people get the correct information.

  Mayor Avalos extended condolences to Council Member Davila. She
  attended the Backpack giveaway and the Pink Patch Dodger Game and
  described her experience. She commended the Finance Department for
  their award. She described a dinner with Mayor Karen Bass and the topic
  of discussion was the homeless issue and how they can work together to
  address the issue.

CONSENT CALENDAR  Agenda Items 3, 4, 5, 6, 7, 8 and 9 were approved by motion of Council
  Member Rios and seconded by Council Member Davila. Item 2 was pulled
  for separate discussion after consideration of the warrants.

  ROLL CALL: Council Member Davila, yes; Council Member Rios, yes;
  Vice Mayor Hurtado, yes; Mayor Avalos, yes; Council Member Barron,
  absent.

3
PERSONNEL - MOU BETW
CITY & EMPLEE GROUPS  The City Council approved items A & B during Consent Calendar:

  a.  Adopting Resolution No. 2023-56-CC entitled Resolution of the
  City Council of the City of South Gate, California, approving the
  comprehensive successor Memorandum of Understanding (MOU)
  (Contract No. 2023-123-CC) between the City of South Gate and
  the South Gate Police Management Association (SGPMA) for the
  term of July 1, 2021, through June 30, 2025; and

  b.  Authorized the Mayor to execute the comprehensive successor
  Memorandum of Understanding in a form acceptable to the City
  Attorney.

4
PERSONNEL RECRUITMENT
& SELECTION  The City Council adopted Resolution No. 2023-57-CC entitled Resolution
  of the City Council of the City of South Gate, California, amending
  Resolution No. 6454 (Salary Resolution and Position Classification Plan)
  creating the Deputy Director of Public Works - Field Operations position
  in the Public Works Department and authorizing the City Manager to
  eliminate the position of Field Operations Manager when it is vacated
  during Consent Calendar.

  Page 6 of 9
   REGULAR CITY COUNCIL MEETING MINUTES OF AUGUST 22, 2023

PERSONNEL RECRUITMENT
& SELECTION  The City Council adopted Resolution No. 2023-58-CC entitled Resolution
  of the City Council of the City of South Gate, California, amending
  Resolution No. 6454 (Salary Resolution and Position Classification Plan)
  to update the job classification specification for the position of Public
  Works Senior Management Analyst in the Public Works Department
  during Consent Calendar.

6
PERSONNEL RECRUITMENT
& SELECTION  The City Council adopted Resolution No. 2023-59-CC entitled Resolution
  of the City Council of the City of South Gate, California, amending
  Resolution No. 6454 (Salary Resolution and Position Classification Plan)
  by approving the update to the Senior Administrative Analyst (Police)
  classification specification during Consent Calendar.

7
LAW ENFORCEMENT  The City Council approved items A, B & C during Consent Calendar:

  a.  Addendum No. 10 to Contract No. 3130 (Master Equity Lease
  Agreement) with Enterprise FM Trust for a Service Agreement
  with their service provider, Enterprise Fleet Management, Inc., to
  lease a 2023 Nissan Frontier for the Police Department for a term
  of 48 months in the total amount of $41,753;

  b.  Appropriated $3,945 from the unassigned balance of the Asset
  Forfeiture Fund to Account No. 235-570-21-6310 for the first
  annual lease payment; and

  c.  Authorized the Mayor to execute Addendum No. 10 in a form
  acceptable to the City Attorney.

8
PUBLIC ASSISTANCE  The City Council approved items A, B & C during Consent Calendar:

  a.  Master Agreement (Contract No. 2023-124-CC) with the
  Conservation Corp of Long Beach to provide youth employment
  job training, and environmental education through projects offered
  by the City;

  b.  Authorized the Mayor to execute the Agreement in a form
  acceptable to the City Attorney; and

  c.  Authorized the City Manager to approve proposals for projects and
  services under the agreement for up to $300,000.

PARKS  The City Council approved items A & B during Consent Calendar:

  a.  Agreement (Contract No. 2023-125-CC) with Z&K Consultants,
  Inc., to provide construction management and inspection services
  for the construction of the Circle Park Improvement, City Project
  No. 609-PRK, in an amount not to exceed $557,681; and

  b.  Authorized the Mayor to execute the Agreement in a form
  acceptable to the City Attorney.

RECESS  Mayor Avalos announced that Council will take a 3-minute recess.

10
CITY COUNCIL  The City Council approved an Administrative Policy that authorizes the
  City Manager to approve professional services agreements in excess of
  $50,000, in a form approved by the City Attorney for services in
  connection with analyzing and reviewing development applications, where
  such services will be solely funded by the applicant by motion of Council
  Member Davila and seconded by Council Member Rios.

  ROLL CALL: Council Member Davila, yes; Council Member Rios, yes;
  Vice Mayor Hurtado, yes; Mayor Avalos, yes; Council Member Barron,

ADJOURNMENT  Council Member Davila adjourned the meeting in memory of all the lives
